publications.name: ML-Based Behavioral Malware Detection Is Far From a Solved Problem
publications.summary: We presented a quantitative study of how sandbox traces differ from real-world ones, and how it impacts machine learning models. We identified this distribution shift and proposed a solution for ML models that boosted the TPR from 14% to 20%@1%FPR.

publications.name: MAlign: Explainable Static Raw-byte Based Malware Family Classification using Sequence Alignment
publications.summary: We proposed a novel approach, namely MAlign, incorporating concepts from Bioinformatics into Malware Security. We developed a static raw-byte-based malware family classifier with better accuracy and robustness. MAlign also provides explainability by relocating the code blocks responsible for malicious attacks.

publications.name: DRSM: De-Randomized Smoothing on Malware Classifier Providing Certified Robustness
publications.summary: We are the first to propose certified robustness in the domain of static malware detection from executables. We demonstrated both theoretical and empirical robustness of our proposed DRSM framework. Besides, we published a new benign dataset, named PACE.

publications.name: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
publications.summary: We introduced efficient techniques that analyze internal states, attention maps, and output probabilities to detect hallucinations from a single response, significantly improving detection performance, while being less computationally expensive than previous methods.

publications.name: Fast Adversarial Attacks on Language Models In One GPU Minute
publications.summary: We proposed a novel approach in adversarial attack on LLMs, namely BEAST, that can jailbreak, cause hallucination, and membership inference attacks. Our approach can find jailbreaking prompts within one minute under a resource-constrained setting.

publications.name: ProcVQA: Benchmarking the Effects of Structural Properties in Mined Process Visualizations on Vision-Language Model Performance
publications.summary: We introduce ProcVQA, an expert-validated benchmark of procedurally mined process visualizations (linear, tree, graph) with varying structural density, and evaluate 21 VLMs to reveal sharp multi-hop reasoning drops, density-driven extraction hallucinations/errors, and a disconnect between extraction accuracy and reasoning.

publications.name: Adversarial Paraphrasing: A Universal Attack for Humanizing AI-Generated Text
publications.summary: We introduced Adversarial Paraphrasing, a training-free attack framework that universally humanizes any AI-generated text to evade detection more effectively. Our approach leverages an off-the-shelf instruction-following LLM to paraphrase AI-generated content under the guidance of an AI text detector, producing adversarial examples that are specifically optimized to bypass detection.

publications.name: Almost AI, Almost Human: The Challenge of Detecting AI-Polished Writing
publications.summary: We evaluated twelve state-of-the-art AI-text detectors using our created APT-Eval dataset of 15K human-written texts refined to varying degrees with AI tools. We found that detectors often classify even minimally polished text as AI-generated and struggle to distinguish levels of AI involvement.

publications.name: Breaking the Code: Security Assessment of AI Code Agents Through Systematic Jailbreaking Attacks
publications.summary: We introduce JAWS-BENCH, a three-regime benchmark (JAWS-0/1/M) with an executable-aware Judge Framework for assessing code-agent jailbreaks, and evaluate seven LLMs to show ASR rising from 61% (prompt-only) to ~71% (single-file) and ~75% (multi-file, 32% instantly deployable), with agent wrapping increasing vulnerability by 1.6×—motivating execution-aware, code-contextual defenses that preserve refusals.

publications.name: Under the Hood of SKILL.md: Semantic Supply-chain Attacks on AI Agent Skill Registry
publications.summary: We investigate semantic supply-chain risks via SKILL.md-only attacks across three lifecycle stages (Discovery, Selection, Governance), showing that adversarial triggers achieve up to 86% win rates in Discovery, 77.6% selection rates for malicious variants, and 36.5%–100% evasion of governance filters—demonstrating that SKILL.md functions as operational text rather than passive documentation in shaping which capabilities agents find, trust, and execute.
